verses.1:1: The parables of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel,
verses.1:3: for understanding words of prudence, and for receiving the instruction of teaching, righteousness, judgment, and equity,
verses.1:4: so that shrewdness may be given to little ones, and knowledge and understanding to a youth.
verses.1:5: A wise man who listens will be wiser, and one who understands will possess guidance.
verses.1:6: He will perceive a parable and an interpretation, the words of the wise and their riddles.
verses.1:7: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; fools despise wisdom and teaching.
verses.1:8: Listen, my son, to the discipline of your father, and do not abandon the law of your mother,
verses.1:9: so that grace may be added to your head, and a necklace to your neck.
verses.1:10: My son, if sinners entice you, do not yield to them.
verses.1:11: If they say, "Come with us, let us lie in wait for blood; let us hide snares against an innocent man without cause;
verses.1:12: let us swallow him alive like the underworld, and whole like one descending into the pit;
verses.1:13: we will find all precious wealth; we will fill our houses with plunder;
verses.1:14: cast a lot with us, let there be one purse for all of us,"
verses.1:15: my son, do not walk with them; hold back your foot from their paths;
verses.1:16: for their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed blood.
verses.1:17: Yet a net is cast in vain before the eyes of winged creatures.
verses.1:18: They themselves also lie in wait against their own blood, and plot treachery against their own lives.
verses.1:19: Such are the paths of every greedy person: they seize the lives of their possessors.
verses.1:20: Wisdom proclaims outside; in the squares she raises her voice;
verses.1:21: at the head of the crowds she cries out; at the entrances of the city gates she utters her words, saying,
verses.1:22: "How long, little ones, do you love childishness, and will fools desire the things that are harmful to themselves, and will the imprudent hate knowledge?
verses.1:23: Turn back to my reproof. Look, I will bring forth my spirit to you, and I will show my words to you.
verses.1:24: Because I called, and you refused; I stretched out my hand, and there was no one who looked;
verses.1:25: you despised all my counsel, and you neglected my rebukes.
verses.1:26: I also will laugh at your ruin, and I will mock when what you feared comes upon you.
verses.1:27: When sudden calamity rushes in, and ruin strikes like a storm; when affliction and distress come upon you,
verses.1:28: then they will call upon me, and I will not listen; they will rise early in the morning, and they will not find me,
verses.1:29: because they detested discipline, and did not receive the fear of the Lord,
verses.1:30: nor did they yield to my counsel, and they disparaged all my reproof.
verses.1:31: Therefore they will eat the fruits of their own way, and they will be filled with their own counsels.
verses.1:32: The turning away of the little ones will put them to death, and the prosperity of fools will destroy them.
verses.1:33: But whoever listens to me will rest without terror, and will enjoy abundance, with the fear of evils removed."
verses.2:1: My son, if you receive my words, and hide my commandments within yourself,
verses.2:2: so that your ear may hear wisdom, incline your heart to come to know prudence.
verses.2:3: For if you call upon wisdom, and incline your heart to prudence;
verses.2:4: if you seek her like money, and dig her up like treasures,
verses.2:5: then you will understand the fear of the Lord, and you will find the knowledge of God,
verses.2:6: because the Lord gives wisdom, and from His mouth come prudence and knowledge.
verses.2:7: He will guard the salvation of the upright, and protect those who walk guilelessly,
verses.2:8: preserving the paths of righteousness, and guarding the ways of the saints.
verses.2:9: Then you will understand righteousness, judgment, equity, and every good path.
verses.2:10: If wisdom enters your heart, and knowledge pleases your soul,
verses.2:11: counsel will guard you, and prudence will preserve you,
verses.2:12: so that you may be rescued from the evil way, and from the man who speaks perverse things;
verses.2:13: who abandon the straight road, and walk through dark ways;
verses.2:14: who rejoice when they have done evil, and exult in the worst things;
verses.2:15: whose ways are perverse, and their steps are disreputable.
verses.2:16: So that you may be rescued from a strange woman, and from an outsider who softens her words,
verses.2:17: and abandons the guide of her youth,
verses.2:18: and has forgotten the covenant of her God. For her house leans toward death, and her paths toward the underworld.
verses.2:19: None who go in to her will return, nor will they lay hold of the paths of life.
verses.2:20: So that you may walk in the good way, and keep the paths of the righteous:
verses.2:21: for those who are upright will dwell in the land, and the guileless will remain in it;
verses.2:22: but the ungodly will be destroyed from the land, and those who act unjustly will be taken away from it.
verses.3:1: My son, do not forget my law, and let your heart guard my precepts;
verses.3:2: for they will add length of days, years of life, and peace to you.
verses.3:3: Do not let mercy and truth desert you; place them around your neck, and inscribe them on the tablets of your heart,
verses.3:4: and you will find grace and good discipline before God and people.
verses.3:5: Put your confidence in the Lord with your whole heart, and do not rely on your own discernment.
verses.3:6: In all your ways consider Him, and He Himself will direct your steps.
verses.3:7: Do not be wise in your own estimation; fear God, and depart from evil.
verses.3:8: For indeed it will be health to your navel, and a watering of your bones.
verses.3:9: Honor the Lord from your possessions, and from the firstfruits of all your crops give to Him,
verses.3:10: and your storehouses will be filled with plenty, and your winepresses will overflow with wine.
verses.3:11: My son, do not cast aside the discipline of the Lord, nor lose heart when you are corrected by Him;
verses.3:12: for the one whom the Lord loves He corrects, and like a father He takes pleasure in a son.
verses.3:13: Blessed is the person who finds wisdom, and who overflows with discernment.
verses.3:14: Her acquisition is better than the trade of silver, and her fruit than the finest and purest gold.
verses.3:15: She is more precious than all riches, and all things that are desired cannot be compared to her.
verses.3:16: Length of days is in her right hand, and wealth and glory are in her left hand.
verses.3:17: Her ways are lovely ways, and all her paths are peaceful.
verses.3:18: She is a tree of life for those who grasp her, and blessed is the one who holds her fast.
verses.3:19: The Lord founded the earth by wisdom; He established the heavens by discernment.
verses.3:20: By His wisdom the depths burst forth, and the clouds condense with dew.
verses.3:21: My son, do not let these things slip away from your eyes. Guard law and counsel,
verses.3:22: and it will be life for your soul, and grace for your throat.
verses.3:23: Then you will walk confidently on your way, and your foot will not trip.
verses.3:24: If you sleep, you will not be afraid; you will rest, and your sleep will be sweet.
verses.3:25: Do not be frightened by sudden terror, nor by the powers of the wicked rushing upon you.
verses.3:26: For the Lord will be at your side, and He will guard your foot so that you will not be caught.
verses.3:27: Do not prevent the one who is able from doing good; if you have the ability, do good yourself as well.
verses.3:28: Do not say to your friend, "Go and return; tomorrow I will give to you," when you can give immediately.
verses.3:29: Do not plot evil against your friend, while he has confidence in you.
verses.3:30: Do not contend against a person for no reason, when he himself has done no evil to you.
verses.3:31: Do not envy an unjust person, nor imitate his ways,
verses.3:32: because every mocker is an abomination to the Lord, and His conversation is with the straightforward.
verses.3:33: Poverty from the Lord is in the house of the wicked, but the dwellings of the righteous will be blessed.
verses.3:34: He Himself will mock the mockers, and He will give grace to the meek.
verses.3:35: The wise will possess glory; the exaltation of fools is dishonor.
verses.4:1: Listen, sons, to a father's discipline, and pay attention so that you may know discernment.
verses.4:2: I will bestow a good gift on you; do not abandon my law.
verses.4:3: For I too was a son of my father, tender and an only child before my mother.
verses.4:4: And he taught me and said, "Let your heart accept my words; guard my precepts, and you will live.
verses.4:5: Possess wisdom, possess discernment; do not forget, nor turn aside from the words of my mouth.
verses.4:6: Do not let her go, and she will guard you; love her, and she will preserve you.
verses.4:8: Seize her, and she will exalt you; you will be glorified by her when you have embraced her.
verses.4:9: She will give an increase of graces to your head, and she will shield you with a glorious crown."
verses.4:10: Listen, my son, and accept my words, so that years of life may be multiplied for you.
verses.4:11: I will show you the way of wisdom; I will lead you through paths of equity.
verses.4:12: When you have entered them, your steps will not be hemmed in, and as you run you will have no stumbling block.
verses.4:13: Hold fast to discipline, do not let it go; guard it, for it is your life.
verses.4:14: Do not delight in the paths of the wicked, nor let the way of evil people please you.
verses.4:15: Flee from it, and do not pass through it; turn aside, and desert it.
verses.4:16: For they do not sleep unless they have done evil, and sleep is snatched away from them unless they have tripped someone up.
verses.4:17: They eat the bread of wickedness, and they drink the wine of injustice.
verses.4:18: But the path of the righteous goes forward like a radiant light, and grows until the perfect day.
verses.4:19: The way of the wicked is dark; they do not know where they may fall.
verses.4:20: My son, listen closely to my words, and bend your ear to my utterances.
verses.4:21: Do not let them depart from your eyes; guard them in the center of your heart,
verses.4:22: because they are life for those who find them, and health for all flesh.
verses.4:23: With every safeguard preserve your heart, because from it life proceeds.
verses.4:24: Remove a crooked mouth from yourself, and let slandering lips be far from you.
verses.4:25: Let your eyes see what is straight, and let your eyelids go ahead of your steps.
verses.4:26: Direct the path for your feet, and all your ways will be made firm.
verses.4:27: Do not turn aside to the right or to the left; turn your foot away from evil. For the Lord knows the ways that are on the right, but those that are on the left are perverse. He Himself, however, will make your courses straight, and He will lead your journeys forward in peace.
verses.5:1: My son, pay attention to my wisdom, and incline your ear to my prudence,
verses.5:2: so that you may guard thoughts, and your lips may preserve discipline. Do not pay attention to the deceit of a woman;
verses.5:3: for the lips of a prostitute are a dripping honeycomb, and her throat is sleeker than oil,
verses.5:4: yet her end is bitter like wormwood, and sharp like a double-edged sword.
verses.5:5: Her feet descend into death, and her steps penetrate to the underworld.
verses.5:6: They do not walk along the path of life; her steps are wandering and untraceable.
verses.5:7: Now therefore, my son, listen to me, and do not turn away from the words of my mouth.
verses.5:8: Put your way far from her, and do not approach the doors of her house.
verses.5:9: Do not give your honor to strangers, and your years to a cruel one,
verses.5:10: or else outsiders may be filled with your strength, and your labors may be in another's house,
verses.5:11: and you may groan at the end, when you have consumed your flesh and your body, and say,
verses.5:12: "Why did I detest discipline, and did my heart not yield to reproofs,
verses.5:13: nor did I listen to the voice of those teaching me, and did I not incline my ear to teachers?
verses.5:14: I was nearly in all evil, in the midst of the assembly and the congregation."
verses.5:15: Drink water from your cistern, and the flowing waters of your well;
verses.5:16: let your springs be channeled abroad, and divide your waters in the streets.
verses.5:17: Possess them alone, and let strangers not be partners with you.
verses.5:18: May your wellspring be blessed, and be glad with the wife of your youth.
verses.5:19: A dearest doe and a most graceful fawn: may her breasts intoxicate you at all times; take delight in her love continually.
verses.5:20: Why are you led astray, my son, by a foreign woman, and cherished in the bosom of another?
verses.5:21: The Lord looks upon the ways of a man, and examines all his steps.
verses.5:22: His own iniquities capture the ungodly man, and he is bound tightly by the ropes of his sins.
verses.5:23: He himself will die, because he did not have discipline, and in the multitude of his folly he will be deceived.
verses.6:1: My son, if you have become guarantor for your friend, you have fastened your hand with an outsider:
verses.6:2: you have been ensnared by the words of your mouth, and caught by your own statements.
verses.6:3: Therefore do what I say, my son, and free yourself, because you have fallen into the hand of your neighbor. Run about, hurry, rouse your friend.
verses.6:4: Do not give sleep to your eyes, nor let your eyelids doze.
verses.6:5: Rescue yourself like a young doe from the hand, and like a bird from the hand of the bird-catcher.
verses.6:6: Go to the ant, you sluggard, and examine her ways, and learn wisdom.
verses.6:7: Although she has no leader, nor instructor, nor ruler,
verses.6:8: she prepares food for herself in summer, and gathers in the harvest what she may eat.
verses.6:9: How long, sluggard, will you sleep? When will you rise up from your sleep?
verses.6:10: You will sleep a little while, you will doze a little while, you will clasp your hands a little while to sleep;
verses.6:11: and want will come to you like a traveler, and poverty like an armed man. Yet if you are diligent, your harvest will come like a spring, and want will flee far from you.
verses.6:12: An apostate person, a useless man, walks with a perverse mouth;
verses.6:13: he winks with his eyes, scrapes with his foot, speaks with his finger;
verses.6:14: with a crooked heart he devises evil, and at all times he sows quarrels.
verses.6:15: To this man his ruin will come immediately, and suddenly he will be crushed, and he will no longer have a remedy.
verses.6:16: There are six things that the Lord hates, and a seventh His soul detests:
verses.6:17: lofty eyes, a lying tongue, hands pouring out innocent blood,
verses.6:18: a heart devising the most evil thoughts, feet swift to run into evil,
verses.6:19: a deceitful witness bringing forth lies, and the one who sows dissensions among brothers.
verses.6:20: Preserve, my son, the precepts of your father, and do not abandon the law of your mother.
verses.6:21: Bind them continually in your heart, and wrap them around your neck.
verses.6:22: When you walk, let them walk with you; when you sleep, let them guard you; and on waking, speak with them.
verses.6:23: Because the commandment is a lamp, and the law is light, and the reproof of discipline is the way of life,
verses.6:24: so that they may guard you from an evil woman, and from the flattering tongue of a foreign woman.
verses.6:25: Do not let your heart lust after her beauty, and do not be captured by her winks;
verses.6:26: for the price of a prostitute is barely a single loaf of bread, yet a man's wife captures a precious soul.
verses.6:27: Can a man conceal fire in his bosom, so that his clothes do not burn?
verses.6:28: Or walk upon burning coals, so that the soles of his feet are not scorched?
verses.6:29: So is the one who goes in to his neighbor's wife; he will not be clean when he has touched her.
verses.6:30: It is not a great fault when someone steals, for he steals so that he may fill a hungry soul;
verses.6:31: even when caught, he will repay sevenfold, and he will hand over all the property of his house.
verses.6:32: Yet the one who is an adulterer, because of poverty of heart, will destroy his own soul;
verses.6:33: he gathers disgrace and dishonor for himself, and his reproach will not be erased,
verses.6:34: because the jealousy and fury of a husband will not spare on the day of vengeance,
verses.6:35: nor will he yield to anyone's pleas, nor will he accept very many gifts for ransom.
verses.7:1: My son, keep my words, and store up my precepts for yourself. Son,
verses.7:2: guard my commandments, and you will live; and my law like the pupil of your eye.
verses.7:3: Bind it on your fingers; write it on the tablets of your heart.
verses.7:4: Say to wisdom, "You are my sister," and call prudence your friend,
verses.7:5: so that they may keep you from a strange woman, and from a foreign woman who makes her words sweet.
verses.7:6: For from the window of my house I looked out through the lattice,
verses.7:7: and I see little ones; I observe a senseless young man,
verses.7:8: who passes through the street by the corner and walks near the way to her house,
verses.7:9: in the dusk, as the day draws toward evening, in the darkness and gloom of night.
verses.7:10: And look, a woman meets him in the attire of a prostitute, prepared to capture souls; talkative and wandering,
verses.7:11: impatient of quiet, and unable to remain in the house with her feet;
verses.7:12: now outside, now in the streets, now lying in wait by the corners.
verses.7:13: And seizing the young man, she kisses him, and with a brazen face she flatters him, saying:
verses.7:14: "I vowed sacrifices for well-being; today I have paid my vows;
verses.7:15: therefore I have come out to meet you, longing to see you, and I have found you.
verses.7:16: I have woven my couch with cords; I have spread it with embroidered tapestries from Egypt.
verses.7:17: I have sprinkled my bed with myrrh, and aloe, and cinnamon.
verses.7:18: Come, let us be intoxicated with breasts, and let us enjoy desired embraces until the day dawns.
verses.7:19: For the man is not in his house; he has gone away on a very long journey;
verses.7:20: he took a bag of money with him; on the day of the full moon he is going to return to his house."
verses.7:21: She ensnared him with many words, and with the flatteries of her lips she drew him along.
verses.7:22: Immediately he follows her like an ox led to sacrifice, and like a frolicking lamb, and not knowing that he, a fool, is being dragged to bonds,
verses.7:23: until an arrow pierces his liver, just as if a bird hurries to a snare, and does not know that it is a matter of peril to its life.
verses.7:24: Now therefore, my son, listen to me, and pay attention to the words of my mouth.
verses.7:25: Do not let your mind be drawn away in her ways, and do not be deceived by her paths;
verses.7:26: for she has cast down many wounded, and all the strongest have been killed by her.
verses.7:27: Her house is the ways of the underworld, penetrating into the inner recesses of death.
verses.8:1: Does not wisdom call out, and prudence give her voice?
verses.8:2: On the highest and loftiest summits above the way, standing in the middle of the paths,
verses.8:3: beside the gates of the city, at the very doors she speaks, saying:
verses.8:4: "Men, to you I call out, and my voice is to the sons of men.
verses.8:5: Little ones, understand shrewdness; and foolish ones, pay attention.
verses.8:6: Listen, for I am about to speak of great things, and my lips will be opened so that they may proclaim what is right.
verses.8:7: My throat will meditate on truth, and my lips will detest the ungodly.
verses.8:8: All my words are just; there is nothing crooked or perverse in them;
verses.8:9: they are right to those who understand, and equitable to those who find knowledge.
verses.8:10: Receive my discipline, and not money; choose teaching rather than gold;
verses.8:11: for wisdom is better than all the most precious things, and no desirable thing can be compared to her.
verses.8:12: I, wisdom, dwell in counsel, and I am present among learned thoughts.
verses.8:13: The fear of the Lord hates evil; arrogance, and pride, and a crooked way, and a double-tongued mouth I detest.
verses.8:14: Mine are counsel and equity; mine is prudence, mine is strength.
verses.8:15: Through me kings reign, and lawmakers decree what is just;
verses.8:16: through me princes rule, and the powerful decree justice.
verses.8:17: I love those who love me, and those who watch early for me will find me.
verses.8:18: With me are riches and glory, splendid wealth and justice.
verses.8:19: For my fruit is better than gold and precious stone, and my yield than choice silver.
verses.8:20: I walk in the ways of justice, in the middle of the paths of judgment,
verses.8:21: so that I may enrich those who love me, and fill their treasuries.
verses.8:22: The Lord possessed me at the outset of His ways, before He made anything from the beginning.
verses.8:23: From eternity I was ordained, and from ancient times before the earth was made.
verses.8:24: The depths did not yet exist, and I had already been conceived; nor had the springs of waters yet burst forth,
verses.8:25: nor had the mountains yet stood firm with their heavy mass; before the hills I was being brought forth.
verses.8:26: He had not yet made the earth, or the rivers, or the pivots of the world.
verses.8:27: When He was preparing the heavens, I was there; when with a fixed law and circle He was enclosing the depths;
verses.8:28: when He was making the upper air firm above, and was balancing the springs of waters;
verses.8:29: when He was setting its boundary around the sea, and placing a law upon the waters, so that they would not cross their limits; when He was weighing out the foundations of the earth,
verses.8:30: I was with Him, arranging all things. And I was delighted day by day, playing before Him at all times,
verses.8:31: playing in the world; and my delight is to be with the sons of men.
verses.8:32: Now therefore, sons, listen to me: blessed are those who keep my ways.
verses.8:34: Blessed is the man who listens to me, and who watches at my doors daily, and keeps watch at the posts of my doorway.
verses.8:35: Whoever finds me will find life, and will draw salvation from the Lord.
verses.8:36: But whoever sins against me will harm his own soul; all who hate me love death."
verses.9:1: Wisdom built a house for herself; she carved out seven pillars.
verses.9:2: She offered her sacrifices, mixed the wine, and set out her table.
verses.9:3: She sent her maidservants to call out at the citadel and at the walls of the city.
verses.9:4: "If anyone is a little one, let him come to me." And she spoke to the unwise:
verses.9:5: "Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine that I have mixed for you.
verses.9:6: Abandon childishness and live, and walk along the paths of prudence.
verses.9:7: Whoever instructs a mocker brings insult upon himself, and whoever rebukes a wicked person produces a blemish for himself.
verses.9:8: Do not rebuke a mocker, so that he will not hate you; rebuke a wise person, and he will love you.
verses.9:9: Give a wise person an opportunity, and wisdom will be added to him; teach a righteous person, and he will hasten to receive it.
verses.9:10: The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and knowledge of the holy ones is prudence.
verses.9:11: For through me your days will be multiplied, and years of life will be added for you.
verses.9:12: If you are wise, you will be so for your own self; but if you are a scoffer, you alone will bear the evil."
verses.9:13: A foolish and loud woman, full of allurements and knowing nothing at all,
verses.9:14: sat at the doorway of her house, on a seat in a high place of the city,
verses.9:15: to call to those passing along the way and proceeding on their journey:
verses.9:16: "Whoever is a little one, let him turn aside to me." And she spoke to the senseless one:
verses.9:17: "Stolen waters are sweeter, and concealed bread is more delightful."
verses.9:18: And he was unaware that giants are there, and that her banquet guests are in the depths of the underworld.
verses.10:1: A wise son gladdens a father, but a foolish son is the grief of his mother.
verses.10:2: Treasures of wickedness will be of no benefit, but righteousness will deliver from death.
verses.10:3: The Lord will not afflict the soul of the righteous with hunger, and He will overturn the plots of the wicked.
verses.10:4: A slack hand has produced poverty, but the hand of the strong prepares riches. Whoever relies on lies shepherds the winds, and that very same one pursues flying birds.
verses.10:5: Whoever gathers in the harvest is a wise son, but whoever snores in summer is a son of disgrace.
verses.10:6: The blessing of the Lord is on the head of the righteous, but iniquity covers the mouth of the wicked.
verses.10:7: The memory of the righteous is with praises, and the name of the wicked will decay.
verses.10:8: The wise in heart receives precepts; a fool in his lips is beaten.
verses.10:9: Whoever walks sincerely walks confidently, but whoever perverts his ways will be exposed.
verses.10:10: Whoever winks with the eye will cause pain, and a fool in his lips will be lashed.
verses.10:11: A wellspring of life is the mouth of the righteous, and the mouth of the wicked covers iniquity.
verses.10:12: Hatred stirs up quarrels, and love covers all misdeeds.
verses.10:13: On the lips of the wise, wisdom is found, and a rod is on the back of the one who lacks sense.
verses.10:14: The wise conceal knowledge, but the mouth of a fool is very close to disgrace.
verses.10:15: The wealth of a rich person is the city of his strength; the terror of the poor is their poverty.
verses.10:16: The work of the righteous leads to life, but the fruit of the wicked to sin.
verses.10:17: The way of life is for the one who keeps discipline, but whoever abandons reproofs goes astray.
verses.10:18: Lying lips conceal hatred; whoever utters insult is unwise.
verses.10:19: In much speaking sin will not be lacking, but whoever restrains his lips is most prudent.
verses.10:20: Choice silver is the tongue of the righteous, but the heart of the wicked counts for nothing.
verses.10:21: The lips of the righteous instruct very many, but those who are untaught will die in poverty of mind.
verses.10:22: The blessing of the Lord makes people rich, and affliction will not be joined to them.
verses.10:23: As if for a laugh, a fool commits a wicked deed, but wisdom is prudence for a man.
verses.10:24: What the wicked person fears will come upon him; the righteous person will be granted his desire.
verses.10:25: Like a passing storm, the wicked person will be no more, but the righteous person is like an everlasting foundation.
verses.10:26: Just as vinegar is to the teeth and smoke is to the eyes, so is a lazy person to those who sent him.
verses.10:27: The fear of the Lord will add days, and the years of the wicked will be shortened.
verses.10:28: The expectation of the righteous is gladness, but the hope of the wicked will perish.
verses.10:29: The strength of the sincere person is the way of the Lord, and it is terror to those who work evil.
verses.10:30: The righteous person will never be shaken, but the wicked will not dwell on the earth.
verses.10:31: The mouth of the righteous will give birth to wisdom; the tongue of the perverse will perish.
verses.10:32: The lips of the righteous consider pleasing things, and the mouth of the wicked, perverse things.
verses.11:1: A deceitful scale is an abomination before the Lord, and a fair weight is His pleasure.
verses.11:2: Where pride is, there disgrace will also be; but where humility is, wisdom is there as well.
verses.11:3: The sincerity of the righteous will direct them, and the treachery of the perverse will devastate them.
verses.11:5: The righteousness of the sincere person will direct his way, and the wicked person will fall in his own wickedness.
verses.11:6: The righteousness of the upright will deliver them, and the unjust will be captured in their own ambushes.
verses.11:7: When a wicked person dies, there will no longer be any hope, and the expectation of the anxious will perish.
verses.11:8: The righteous person has been delivered from distress, and the wicked person will be handed over in his place.
verses.11:9: The hypocrite deceives his friend with his mouth, but the righteous will be delivered by knowledge.
verses.11:10: At the prosperity of the righteous the city will exult, and at the destruction of the wicked there will be praise.
verses.11:11: Through the blessing of the righteous the city will be exalted, and by the mouth of the wicked it will be overturned.
verses.11:12: Whoever despises his friend is lacking in heart, but a prudent man will keep silent.
verses.11:13: Whoever walks fraudulently reveals secrets, but one who is faithful in spirit conceals what a friend has entrusted.
verses.11:14: Where there is no helmsman, the people will fall; but there is safety where there are many counsels.
verses.11:15: Whoever gives a pledge for a stranger will be afflicted with harm, but whoever guards against snares will be secure.
verses.11:16: A gracious woman will find glory, and the mighty will possess wealth.
verses.11:17: A merciful man does good to his own soul, but whoever is cruel rejects even his relatives.
verses.11:18: The wicked person does unstable work, but for the one who sows righteousness there is a sure reward.
verses.11:19: Clemency prepares life, and the pursuit of evil prepares death.
verses.11:20: A crooked heart is abominable to the Lord, and His pleasure is in those who walk in sincerity.
verses.11:21: Hand in hand, an evil person will not be guiltless, but the offspring of the righteous will be saved.
verses.11:22: A gold ring in a pig's snout: a beautiful and foolish woman.
verses.11:23: The desire of the righteous is wholly good; the anticipation of the wicked is wrath.
verses.11:24: Some share out what is their own and become richer; others seize what is not theirs and are always in poverty.
verses.11:25: The soul that blesses will be enriched, and the one who satisfies with drink will himself also be satisfied.
verses.11:26: Whoever hides grain will be cursed among the peoples, but a blessing will be upon the head of those who sell.
verses.11:27: Whoever seeks good things rises well at dawn, but whoever is a searcher of evil things will be overwhelmed by them.
verses.11:28: Whoever trusts in his wealth will fall, but the righteous will sprout like a green leaf.
verses.11:29: Whoever disrupts his own house will possess the winds, and whoever is a fool will serve one who is wise.
verses.11:30: The fruit of the righteous person is a tree of life, and whoever receives souls is wise.
verses.11:31: If the righteous person receives repayment on earth, how much more the wicked person and the sinner!
verses.12:1: One who loves discipline loves knowledge, but one who hates rebukes is unwise.
verses.12:2: Whoever is good will draw grace from the Lord, but whoever trusts in his own thoughts acts wickedly.
verses.12:3: A person will not be made strong by wickedness, and the root of the righteous will not be shaken.
verses.12:4: A diligent wife is a crown for her husband, and she who does things deserving of shame is decay in his bones.
verses.12:5: The thoughts of the righteous are judgments, and the plans of the wicked are fraudulent.
verses.12:6: The words of the wicked lie in ambush for blood; the mouth of the righteous will deliver them.
verses.12:7: Overturn the wicked, and they will not be; but the house of the righteous will endure.
verses.12:8: By his learning a man will be known, but whoever is empty and senseless will lie open to contempt.
verses.12:9: Better is someone poor and self-sufficient than someone boastful and lacking bread.
verses.12:10: The righteous person knows the lives of his livestock, but the mercies of the wicked are cruel.
verses.12:11: Whoever works his own land will be satisfied with bread, but whoever pursues idleness is utterly foolish. Whoever delights in lingering over wine leaves behind disgrace in his own strongholds.
verses.12:12: The desire of the wicked person is a stronghold of the most evil, but the root of the righteous will thrive.
verses.12:13: Because of the sins of the lips, ruin approaches the evil person, but the righteous person will escape from distress.
verses.12:14: From the fruit of his own mouth each one will be filled with good things, and according to the works of his hands he will be repaid.
verses.12:15: A fool's way is right in his eyes, but whoever is wise listens to counsels.
verses.12:16: A fool immediately discloses his anger, but whoever overlooks a wrong is shrewd.
verses.12:17: Whoever speaks what he knows is a witness to righteousness, but whoever lies is a fraudulent witness.
verses.12:18: There is one who promises and is pierced as if by a sword of conscience, yet the tongue of the wise is health.
verses.12:19: The lip of truth will be firm forever, but whoever is a hasty witness fabricates a tongue of falsehood.
verses.12:20: Deceit is in the heart of those who plot evil things, but joy follows those who enter into plans of peace.
verses.12:21: Whatever happens to the righteous person will not sadden him, but the wicked will be filled with harm.
verses.12:22: False lips are an abomination to the Lord, but those who act faithfully please Him.
verses.12:23: An experienced person conceals knowledge, and the heart of the unwise calls forth folly.
verses.12:24: The hand of the strong will rule, but the one that is slack will serve under tribute.
verses.12:25: Sorrow in a man's heart will humble him, and he will be gladdened by a good word.
verses.12:26: Whoever disregards loss for the sake of a friend is righteous, but the path of the wicked will deceive them.
verses.12:27: A fraudulent person will not find gain, and a person's property will be the value of gold.
verses.12:28: On the pathway of righteousness is life, but a wayward path leads to death.
verses.13:1: A wise son is a father's instruction, but he who is a mocker does not listen when he is rebuked.
verses.13:2: From the fruit of his own mouth a man will be satisfied with good things, but the soul of transgressors is unjust.
verses.13:3: He who guards his mouth guards his soul, but he who is thoughtless in speaking will experience evil.
verses.13:4: The lazy man wants and does not want, but the soul of those who work will be made fat.
verses.13:5: The righteous man will detest a lying word, but the wicked man puts to shame and will be put to shame.
verses.13:6: Righteousness guards the way of the innocent, but wickedness trips up the sinner.
verses.13:7: There is one who is as if rich, though he has nothing, and there is one who is as if poor, though he is in great riches.
verses.13:8: A man's own riches are the ransom of his soul, but he who is poor does not endure a rebuke.
verses.13:9: The light of the righteous brings gladness, but the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
verses.13:10: Among the proud there are always quarrels, but those who do all things with counsel are governed by wisdom.
verses.13:11: Wealth gained in haste will diminish, but what is gathered little by little by hand will be multiplied.
verses.13:12: Hope that is delayed afflicts the soul; a desire that arrives is a tree of life.
verses.13:13: He who disparages any matter binds himself for the future, but he who fears the command will live in peace. Deceitful souls go astray in sins, but the righteous are merciful and show mercy.
verses.13:14: The law of a wise man is a fountain of life, so that he may turn aside from the ruin of death.
verses.13:15: Good instruction will give favor; in the path of despisers there is a chasm.
verses.13:16: The shrewd man does all things with counsel, but he who is senseless exposes foolishness.
verses.13:17: The messenger of a wicked man will fall into evil, but a faithful envoy is health.
verses.13:18: Poverty and disgrace are for him who abandons discipline, but he who yields to one who rebukes will be glorified.
verses.13:19: A desire, if it is fulfilled, delights the soul; fools detest those who flee from evil.
verses.13:20: He who walks with the wise will be wise; the friend of fools will become like them.
verses.13:21: Evil pursues sinners, and good things will be repaid to the righteous.
verses.13:22: A good man leaves children and grandchildren as heirs, and the wealth of the sinner is kept for the righteous.
verses.13:23: Much food is in the newly tilled fields of the fathers, and it is gathered for others without justice.
verses.13:24: He who spares the rod hates his own son, but he who loves him instructs him persistently.
verses.13:25: The righteous man eats and fills his soul, but the belly of the wicked is insatiable.
verses.14:1: A wise woman builds her house, but an unwise one will tear down with her hands even one already built.
verses.14:2: He who walks on a straight path and fears God is despised by him who walks in a disgraceful way.
verses.14:3: In the mouth of a fool is a rod of pride, but the lips of the wise guard them.
verses.14:4: Where there are no oxen, the manger is empty; but where there are abundant crops, there the strength of the ox is evident.
verses.14:5: A faithful witness does not lie, but a deceitful witness utters a lie.
verses.14:6: A scoffer seeks wisdom and does not find it; the instruction of the prudent is easy.
verses.14:7: Go against a foolish man, and he does not know lips of prudence.
verses.14:8: The wisdom of an astute man is to understand his own way, and the imprudence of fools goes astray.
verses.14:9: A fool will mock sin, and among the righteous favor will dwell.
verses.14:10: The heart that knows the bitterness of its own soul: a stranger will not mingle in its joy.
verses.14:11: The house of the wicked will be wiped out, but the tents of the righteous will sprout.
verses.14:12: There is a way that appears right to a man, but its final ends lead down to death.
verses.14:13: Laughter will be mingled with sorrow, and mourning seizes the end of joy.
verses.14:14: A fool will be filled with his own ways, and a good man will be above him.
verses.14:15: An innocent man believes every word; a shrewd man considers his steps. For a deceitful son there will be nothing good, but for a wise servant his deeds will be prosperous, and his way will be directed.
verses.14:16: A wise man fears and turns aside from evil; a fool oversteps and is confident.
verses.14:17: An impatient man will work foolishness, and a crafty man is odious.
verses.14:18: Little ones will possess foolishness, and the shrewd will wait for knowledge.
verses.14:19: The evil will lie prostrate before the good, and the wicked before the gates of the righteous.
verses.14:20: Even to his own neighbor a poor man will be odious, but the friends of the rich are many.
verses.14:21: He who despises his neighbor sins, but he who shows mercy to the poor will be blessed. He who believes in the Lord loves mercy.
verses.14:22: Those who work evil go astray; mercy and truth prepare good things.
verses.14:23: In all work there will be abundance, but where words are very many, there is frequently poverty.
verses.14:24: The crown of the wise is their riches; the folly of fools is imprudence.
verses.14:25: A faithful witness delivers souls, and a two-faced man utters lies.
verses.14:26: In the fear of the Lord is confidence of strength, and for His children there will be hope.
verses.14:27: The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life, so that they may turn aside from the ruin of death.
verses.14:28: In a multitude of people is the dignity of a king, and in a scarcity of the populace is the disgrace of a prince.
verses.14:29: He who is patient is governed by great prudence, but he who is impatient exalts his own foolishness.
verses.14:30: The life of the flesh is health of the heart; decay of the bones is envy.
verses.14:31: He who slanders the needy reproaches his Maker, but he who shows mercy to the poor honors Him.
verses.14:32: In his malice the wicked man will be driven out, but the righteous man has hope in his death.
verses.14:33: In the heart of a prudent man wisdom rests, and it will instruct all the unlearned.
verses.14:34: Righteousness lifts up a nation, but sin makes peoples wretched.
verses.14:35: An understanding minister is acceptable to a king; a worthless one will endure his wrath.
verses.15:1: A soft reply breaks anger; a harsh word arouses fury.
verses.15:2: The tongue of the wise adorns knowledge; the mouth of the senseless bubbles over with folly.
verses.15:3: In every place, the eyes of the Lord observe the good and the evil.
verses.15:4: A calming tongue is a tree of life, but one that is unrestrained will crush the spirit.
verses.15:5: A fool mocks his father's discipline, but the one who keeps rebukes will become more astute. In abundant righteousness there is the greatest strength, but the thoughts of the wicked will be uprooted.
verses.15:6: The house of the righteous is very great strength, and in the fruits of the wicked there is turmoil.
verses.15:7: The lips of the wise will spread knowledge; the heart of fools will be different.
verses.15:8: The sacrifices of the wicked are abominable to the Lord; the vows of the righteous are pleasing.
verses.15:9: An abomination to the Lord is the way of the wicked; the one who follows righteousness is loved by Him.
verses.15:10: Harsh instruction is for the one who abandons the way of life; the one who hates rebukes will die.
verses.15:11: The underworld and destruction are before the Lord; how much more the hearts of the sons of men!
verses.15:12: A pestilent person does not love the one who reproves him, nor does he go to the wise.
verses.15:13: A rejoicing heart brightens the face; in sorrow of mind the spirit is brought low.
verses.15:14: The heart of the wise seeks instruction, and the mouth of fools feeds on ignorance.
verses.15:15: All the days of the poor are bad; an untroubled mind is like a continual banquet.
verses.15:16: A little with the fear of the Lord is better than great and insatiable treasures.
verses.15:17: It is better to be invited to vegetables with love than to a fattened calf with hatred.
verses.15:18: A quick-tempered man provokes quarrels; the one who is patient calms those that have been aroused.
verses.15:19: The road of the lazy is like a hedge of thorns; the way of the righteous is without obstacle.
verses.15:20: A wise son gladdens a father, and a foolish man despises his own mother.
verses.15:21: Folly is a joy for a fool, and a prudent man directs his own steps.
verses.15:22: Plans are scattered where there is no counsel, but where there are many counselors, they are confirmed.
verses.15:23: A man rejoices in the utterance of his mouth, and a timely word is best.
verses.15:24: The path of life is above a learned man, so that he may turn away from the lowest underworld.
verses.15:25: The Lord will demolish the house of the proud, and will make firm the boundaries of the widow.
verses.15:26: An abomination to the Lord are evil thoughts, and pure, most beautiful speech will be established by Him.
verses.15:27: The one who pursues greed throws his own house into turmoil, but the one who hates bribes will live. Through mercy and faith sins are cleansed, and through the fear of the Lord everyone turns away from evil.
verses.15:28: The mind of the righteous meditates on obedience; the mouth of the wicked overflows with evil things. When the ways of a man please the Lord, He will turn even his enemies to peace.
verses.15:29: The Lord is far away from the wicked, and He will hear the prayers of the righteous. A little with righteousness is better than many fruits with unrighteousness.
verses.15:30: The light of the eyes gladdens the soul; a good report fattens the bones.
verses.15:32: The one who casts aside discipline despises his own soul, but the one who yields to rebukes is a possessor of a heart.
verses.15:33: The fear of the Lord is the discipline of wisdom, and humility precedes glory.
verses.16:2: All the ways of a man lie open to his eyes; the weigher of spirits is the Lord.
verses.16:5: An abomination to the Lord is every arrogant person; even if hand joins hand, he is not innocent. The beginning of a good way is doing righteousness, and it is more acceptable with God than offering sacrifices.
verses.16:9: The Lord has made everything for His own sake, even the wicked for the evil day.
verses.16:10: Divination is on the lips of a king; in judgment his mouth will not err.
verses.16:11: A weight and a balance are the Lord's judgments, and His works are all the stones of the pouch.
verses.16:12: Abominable to a king are those who act wickedly, because by righteousness a throne is established.
verses.16:13: Righteous lips are the pleasure of kings; the one who speaks what is right will be loved.
verses.16:14: A king's indignation is messengers of death, and a wise man will appease it.
verses.16:15: In the cheerfulness of a king's face there is life, and his clemency is like a late rain.
verses.16:16: Possess wisdom, because it is better than gold, and acquire prudence, because it is more precious than silver.
verses.16:17: The path of the righteous turns away from evils; the guardian of his own soul keeps his way.
verses.16:18: Pride precedes destruction, and before ruin the spirit is lifted up.
verses.16:19: It is better to be humbled with the gentle than to divide plunder with the proud.
verses.16:20: The one learned in the word will find good things, and the one who hopes in the Lord is blessed.
verses.16:21: The one who is wise in heart will be called prudent, and the one who is sweet in speech will receive greater things.
verses.16:22: Learning is a fountain of life to its possessor; the instruction of fools is senselessness.
verses.16:23: The heart of a wise man will teach his mouth, and to his lips it will add grace.
verses.16:24: Well-arranged words are a honeycomb, sweetness of the soul, health of the bones.
verses.16:25: There is a way that appears right to a man, and its final ends lead to death.
verses.16:26: The soul of the one who labors labors for itself, because his mouth has compelled him.
verses.16:27: A wicked man digs up evil, and on his lips a fire blazes.
verses.16:28: A perverse man arouses disputes, and a talkative man separates princes.
verses.16:29: An unrighteous man entices his friend, and leads him along a way that is not good.
verses.16:30: The one who with staring eyes plots crooked things, biting his own lips, accomplishes evil.
verses.16:31: A crown of dignity is old age, which will be found in the ways of righteousness.
verses.16:32: A patient person is better than a strong man, and the one who masters his own mind than a conqueror of cities.
verses.16:33: Lots are cast into the lap, but they are governed by the Lord.
verses.17:1: A dry morsel with joy is better than a house full of sacrifices with quarreling.
verses.17:2: A wise servant will rule over foolish sons and will divide the inheritance among the brothers.
verses.17:3: Just as silver is tested by fire and gold in the furnace, so the Lord tests hearts.
verses.17:4: An evil man obeys an unjust tongue, and a deceitful man complies with lying lips.
verses.17:5: Whoever despises a poor man reproaches his Maker, and whoever rejoices in the ruin of another will not go unpunished.
verses.17:6: The crown of old men is children's children, and the glory of children is their fathers.
verses.17:7: Well-ordered words are not fitting for a fool, nor is a lying lip for a prince.
verses.17:8: The expectation of one who waits is a most pleasing gem; wherever he turns, he understands prudently.
verses.17:9: Whoever conceals an offense seeks friendships; whoever repeats it with a second remark separates allies.
verses.17:10: A rebuke accomplishes more with a prudent man than a hundred blows with a fool.
verses.17:11: An evil man always seeks quarrels, yet a cruel angel will be sent against him.
verses.17:12: It is preferable to meet a she-bear robbed of her cubs than a simpleton trusting in his folly.
verses.17:13: Whoever repays evil for good, evil will not withdraw from his house.
verses.17:14: Whoever releases water is the beginning of quarrels, and before he suffers insult, he abandons judgment.
verses.17:15: Whoever justifies the wicked, and whoever condemns the righteous, each of them is abominable before God.
verses.17:16: What does it profit a fool to have riches, since he cannot buy wisdom? Whoever makes his house high seeks ruin, and whoever avoids learning will fall into evils.
verses.17:17: One who is a friend loves at all times, and a brother is proven in times of distress.
verses.17:18: A foolish man will clap his hands when he pledges himself for his friend.
verses.17:19: Whoever meditates on dissensions loves disputes, and whoever raises a doorway high seeks ruin.
verses.17:20: Whoever has a perverse heart will not find good, and whoever twists his tongue will fall into evil.
verses.17:21: A fool is born to his own disgrace, and not even a father will rejoice in a simpleton.
verses.17:22: A joyful mind makes a flourishing life; a sorrowful spirit dries up the bones.
verses.17:23: A wicked man accepts gifts from the bosom so that he may pervert the paths of judgment.
verses.17:24: On the face of a prudent man wisdom shines; the eyes of fools are at the ends of the earth.
verses.17:25: A foolish son is a father's anger and the grief of the mother who gave birth to him.
verses.17:26: It is not good to inflict loss upon a righteous man, nor to strike a prince who judges what is right.
verses.17:27: Whoever moderates his words is learned and prudent, and a well-instructed man has a precious spirit.
verses.17:28: Even a fool, if he keeps silent, will be counted wise, and if he presses his lips shut, intelligent.
verses.18:1: Whoever wants to withdraw from a friend seeks pretexts; at all times he will be worthy of reproach.
verses.18:2: A fool does not accept words of prudence, unless you say the things that revolve in his heart.
verses.18:3: The wicked man, when he comes into the depth of sins, shows contempt; yet disgrace and reproach follow him.
verses.18:4: Words from a man's mouth are deep water, and the spring of wisdom is an overflowing torrent.
verses.18:5: Showing partiality to a wicked man is not good, so that you turn aside from the truth of judgment.
verses.18:6: The lips of a fool entangle themselves in disputes, and his mouth provokes quarrels.
verses.18:7: A fool's mouth is his destruction, and his own lips are the ruin of his soul.
verses.18:8: The words of a double-tongued man are as though simple, and they themselves reach all the way to the innermost parts of the belly. Fear casts down the lazy man, and the souls of the effeminate will go hungry.
verses.18:9: Whoever is soft and slack in his work is the brother of one who destroys his own works.
verses.18:10: The name of the Lord is a very strong tower; the righteous man runs to it and will be exalted.
verses.18:11: The wealth of a rich man is the city of his strength, and like a strong wall surrounding him.
verses.18:12: Before it is crushed, a man's heart is exalted, and before it is glorified, it is humbled.
verses.18:13: Whoever answers before he hears proves himself to be a fool and worthy of shame.
verses.18:14: The spirit of a man sustains his weakness, but who will be able to endure a spirit that is easily angered?
verses.18:15: A prudent heart will possess knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks teaching.
verses.18:16: A man's gift widens his way and makes room for him before princes.
verses.18:17: The righteous man is the first accuser of himself; his friend comes and will search him out.
verses.18:18: The lot suppresses controversies and decides even between the powerful.
verses.18:19: A brother who is helped by a brother is like a fortified city, and judgments are like the bars of cities.
verses.18:20: From the fruit of a man's mouth his belly will be filled, and the yield of his own lips will satisfy him.
verses.18:21: Death and life are in the hand of the tongue; those who love it will eat its fruits.
verses.18:22: Whoever finds a good wife finds a good thing, and will draw delight from the Lord. Whoever drives out a good wife drives out a good thing, yet whoever keeps an adulteress is foolish and wicked.
verses.19:3: A person's folly trips up his steps, and he seethes in his spirit against God.
verses.19:4: Wealth adds very many friends, but from a poor man even those whom he had separate themselves.
verses.19:5: A false witness will not remain unpunished, and the one who speaks lies will not escape.
verses.19:6: Many pay court to the person of a powerful man, and they are friends of the one who gives gifts.
verses.19:7: The brothers of a poor man hate him; moreover, even friends have withdrawn far from him. The one who pursues only words will have nothing.
verses.19:8: But the one who possesses understanding loves his own soul, and the keeper of prudence will find good things.
verses.19:9: A false witness will not remain unpunished, and the one who speaks lies will perish.
verses.19:10: Luxuries are not proper for a fool, nor is it proper for a servant to rule over princes.
verses.19:11: A man's learning is recognized through patience, and his glory is to pass over injustices.
verses.19:12: Like the growling of a lion, so also is a king's anger, and like dew on the grass, so also is his cheerfulness.
verses.19:13: A foolish son is a father's grief, and a quarrelsome woman is a continually dripping roof.
verses.19:14: A house and wealth are given by parents, but a prudent wife is specifically from the Lord.
verses.19:15: Laziness brings on deep sleep, and a slack soul will go hungry.
verses.19:16: The one who keeps the commandment keeps his own soul, but the one who neglects his way will be put to death.
verses.19:17: The one who has mercy on a poor man lends to the Lord, and He will pay him his recompense.
verses.19:18: Train your son; do not despair, yet do not set your soul toward killing him.
verses.19:19: The one who is impatient will endure loss, and when he takes by force, he will add something else.
verses.19:20: Hear counsel and receive discipline, so that you may be wise in your final days.
verses.19:21: Many are the thoughts in a man's heart, but the will of the Lord will endure.
verses.19:22: A needy person is merciful, and a poor man is better than a lying man.
verses.19:23: The fear of the Lord leads to life, and he will dwell in fullness without a most evil visitation.
verses.19:24: The lazy man hides his hand under his armpit, and does not bring it to his mouth.
verses.19:25: When a pestilent man is flogged, the fool will become wiser; but if you rebuke a wise man, he will understand discipline.
verses.19:26: The one who afflicts his father and drives away his mother is disgraceful and wretched.
verses.19:27: Do not cease, son, to listen to instruction, nor be ignorant of the words of knowledge.
verses.19:28: An unjust witness mocks judgment, and the mouth of the wicked devours injustice.
verses.19:29: Judgments are prepared for mockers, and beating hammers for the bodies of fools.
verses.20:1: Wine is a wanton thing, and drunkenness is tumultuous; whoever delights in these will not be wise.
verses.20:2: Like the roaring of a lion, so also is the terror of a king; the one who provokes him sins against his own soul.
verses.20:3: It is an honor for a person who separates himself from disputes, but all fools meddle in insults.
verses.20:4: Because of the cold the lazy man was unwilling to plow; therefore he will beg in the summer, and nothing will be given to him.
verses.20:5: Like deep water, so is counsel in a man's heart, but a wise person will draw it out.
verses.20:6: Many people are called merciful, but who will find a faithful man?
verses.20:7: The righteous man who walks in his simplicity will leave blessed children after him.
verses.20:8: A king who sits on the throne of judgment scatters all evil with his gaze.
verses.20:9: Who is able to say, "My heart is clean; I am pure from sin"? The one who curses his father and mother, his lamp will be extinguished in the midst of darkness; an inheritance toward which one hurries at the beginning will lack a blessing in the end. Do not say, "I will pay back evil." Wait for the Lord, and He will rescue you.
verses.20:10: A weight and a weight, a measure and a measure: both are abominable before God.
verses.20:11: By his pursuits a boy is understood, whether his works are clean and upright.
verses.20:12: An ear that hears and an eye that sees: the Lord made both.
verses.20:13: Do not love sleep, so that poverty may not overwhelm you; open your eyes, and be satisfied with bread.
verses.20:23: A weight and a weight is an abomination before the Lord; a deceitful scale is not good.
verses.20:24: A man's steps are directed by the Lord, but who among people can understand his own way?
verses.20:25: It is ruin for a person to devour holy ones, and to draw back after vows.
verses.20:26: A wise king scatters the wicked, and bends an arch over them.
verses.20:27: The breath of a person is the lamp of the Lord, which searches out all the hidden recesses of the belly.
verses.20:28: Mercy and truth keep a king, and by clemency his throne is made strong.
verses.20:29: The exultation of young men is their strength, and the dignity of old men is gray hair.
verses.20:30: The bruise of a wound will wipe away evils, and blows in the deeper recesses of the belly.
verses.21:1: Like divisions of water, so is a king's heart in the hand of the Lord; wherever He wills, He will turn it.
verses.21:2: Every way of a man appears right to himself, but the Lord weighs hearts.
verses.21:3: To practice mercy and justice pleases the Lord more than sacrifices.
verses.21:4: Haughtiness of the eyes is swelling of the heart; the lamp of the wicked is sin.
verses.21:6: One who gathers treasures by a lying tongue is empty and senseless, and will be driven into the snares of death.
verses.21:7: The robberies of the wicked will drag them down, because they refused to practice justice.
verses.21:8: A man's perverse way is foreign, while the work of one who is pure is upright.
verses.21:9: It is better to sit in a corner of a rooftop than with a quarrelsome woman and in a shared house.
verses.21:10: The soul of a wicked man desires evil; he will show no mercy to his neighbor.
verses.21:11: When a pestilent person is punished, a little one will grow wiser; and if he pursues a wise person, he will gain knowledge.
verses.21:12: A righteous man reflects carefully on the house of a wicked man, so that he may draw the wicked away from evil.
verses.21:13: Whoever blocks his ear to the cry of the poor will himself also cry out, and will not be heard.
verses.21:14: A hidden gift extinguishes fits of anger, and a present in the bosom, the greatest indignation.
verses.21:15: It is a joy for a righteous person to practice justice, and terror for those who work iniquity.
verses.21:16: A man who strays from the way of instruction will dwell in the assembly of the giants.
verses.21:17: Whoever loves banquets will be in poverty; whoever loves wine and rich foods will not grow rich.
verses.21:18: A wicked man is given in place of a righteous man, and an unjust man in place of the upright.
verses.21:19: It is better to dwell in a desert land than with an argumentative and hot-tempered woman.
verses.21:20: Desirable treasure and oil are in the dwelling of a righteous man, and an imprudent person will squander it.
verses.21:21: One who follows righteousness and mercy will find life, righteousness, and glory.
verses.21:22: A wise man scaled the city of the strong and tore down the strength of its confidence.
verses.21:23: The one who guards his mouth and his tongue guards his soul from distresses.
verses.21:24: A proud and arrogant man is called uninstructed, the one who works pride in anger.
verses.21:25: Desires kill the lazy man, for his hands have refused to do any work.
verses.21:26: All day long he craves and desires, while the one who is righteous will give and will not cease.
verses.21:27: The sacrifices of the wicked are detestable, because they are offered from wrongdoing.
verses.21:28: A lying witness will perish; an obedient man will speak victory.
verses.21:29: A wicked man brazenly hardens his face, while the one who is upright corrects his way.
verses.21:30: There is no wisdom, there is no discernment, there is no plan against the Lord.
verses.21:31: A horse is made ready for the day of battle, but the Lord grants deliverance.
verses.22:1: A good name is better than abundant wealth; above silver and gold is good favor.
verses.22:2: The rich person and the poor person have met each other; the Lord is the maker of both.
verses.22:3: A shrewd person saw evil and hid himself; an innocent person went right on and was afflicted with loss.
verses.22:4: The outcome of humility is the fear of the Lord, wealth, glory, and life.
verses.22:5: Weapons and swords are in the way of the perverse person, yet the guardian of his own soul withdraws far from them.
verses.22:7: A rich man rules over the poor, and whoever takes a loan is a slave to the lender.
verses.22:8: Whoever sows iniquity will reap evils, and the rod of his anger will be brought to an end.
verses.22:9: Whoever is inclined to mercy will be blessed, for he has given from his own bread to the poor. The one who gives gifts will acquire victory and honor, yet he takes away the soul of the recipients.
verses.22:10: Drive out the mocker, and quarreling will go out with him, and disputes and insults will cease.
verses.22:11: One who loves purity of heart, because of the grace of his lips, will have the king as a friend.
verses.22:12: The eyes of the Lord guard knowledge, and the words of an unjust man are overturned.
verses.22:13: The lazy man says, "There is a lion outside; in the middle of the streets I am going to be killed."
verses.22:14: A deep pit is the mouth of a foreign woman; the one with whom the Lord is angry will fall into it.
verses.22:15: Folly is bound tightly in a child's heart, and the rod of discipline will chase it away.
verses.22:16: One who falsely accuses the poor in order to increase his own wealth will himself give to one who is richer, and will be in need.
verses.22:17: Incline your ear and listen to the words of the wise, and apply your heart to my instruction,
verses.22:18: which will be beautiful to you when you keep it inside your belly, and it will overflow on your lips:
verses.22:19: so that your confidence may be in the Lord, for which reason I have also shown it to you today.
verses.22:20: Look, I have written it out for you in a threefold way, in thoughts and knowledge:
verses.22:21: so that I might show you reliability and utterances of truth, to answer from these to those who sent you.
verses.22:22: Do not do violence to a poor person because he is poor, nor crush the needy in the gate:
verses.22:23: because the Lord will judge his case, and will pierce those who have pierced his soul.
verses.22:24: Do not be a friend to a hot-tempered person, and do not walk with a furious man:
verses.22:25: so that you might not learn his paths and take a stumbling block for your soul.
verses.22:26: Do not be with those who pledge their hands, and who offer themselves as guarantors for debts:
verses.22:27: for if you do not have the means to repay, what reason is there for him to take the covering from your bed?
verses.22:28: Do not cross over the ancient boundaries that your fathers placed.
verses.22:29: Have you seen a man quick in his work? He will stand before kings, and he will not be before obscure people.
verses.23:1: When you sit to eat with a ruler, pay careful attention to what has been placed before your face.
verses.23:2: And place a knife at your throat, if indeed you have your soul in your power.
verses.23:3: Do not desire any of his foods, in which is bread of falsehood.
verses.23:4: Do not toil to become rich, but place a limit on your prudence.
verses.23:5: Do not lift up your eyes to riches that you cannot have, for they will make wings for themselves like an eagle's, and will fly into the sky.
verses.23:6: Do not eat with an envious man, and do not desire his foods,
verses.23:7: for in the likeness of a fortune-teller and an interpreter of omens, he calculates what he does not know. "Eat and drink," he will say to you, yet his mind is not with you.
verses.23:8: You will vomit up the foods that you had eaten, and you will lose your fine words.
verses.23:9: Do not speak in the ears of the foolish, who will despise the instruction of your discourse.
verses.23:10: Do not touch the boundaries of little ones, and do not enter the field of orphans;
verses.23:11: for their kinsman is strong, and he himself will judge their case against you.
verses.23:12: Let your heart enter into instruction, and your ears to the words of knowledge.
verses.23:13: Do not withhold discipline from a boy; for if you strike him with a rod, he will not die.
verses.23:14: You will strike him with a rod, and you will rescue his soul from hell.
verses.23:15: My son, if your mind is wise, my heart will rejoice with you,
verses.23:16: and my kidneys will exult when your lips speak what is right.
verses.23:17: Do not let your heart envy sinners, but remain in the fear of the Lord all day long;
verses.23:18: for you will have hope in the end, and your expectation will not be taken away.
verses.23:19: Listen, my son, and be wise, and direct your mind in the way.
verses.23:20: Do not be at the banquets of drinkers, nor at the revelries of those who bring meat together to eat;
verses.23:21: for those who devote themselves to drinking and contribute to shared feasts will be consumed, and drowsiness will be clothed in rags.
verses.23:22: Listen to your father who fathered you, and do not despise your mother when she has grown old.
verses.23:24: The father of a righteous man exults with joy; he who has fathered a wise one will be glad in him.
verses.23:25: Let your father and your mother rejoice, and let her who gave birth to you exult.
verses.23:26: Offer your heart to me, my son, and let your eyes guard my ways.
verses.23:27: For a prostitute is a deep pit, and a foreign woman is a narrow well.
verses.23:28: She lies in wait along the way like a robber, and she will kill those whom she sees unwary.
verses.23:29: Who has woe? Whose father has woe? Who has quarrels? Who has pits? Who has wounds without cause? Who has bloodshot eyes?
verses.23:30: Is it not those who linger over wine, and devote themselves to draining cups?
verses.23:31: Do not gaze at wine when it turns golden, when its color gleams in the glass; it goes down smoothly,
verses.23:32: but in the end it will bite like a serpent, and like a basilisk it will pour out venom.
verses.23:33: Your eyes will see foreign women, and your heart will speak perverse things.
verses.23:34: And you will be like one sleeping in the middle of the sea, and like a helmsman overcome with sleep, with the rudder lost.
verses.23:35: And you will say, "They beat me, but I felt no pain; they dragged me, and I did not sense it. When will I wake up and find wine again?"
verses.24:1: Do not envy evil men, nor desire to be with them;
verses.24:2: for their mind plots robberies, and their lips speak frauds.
verses.24:3: A house will be built by wisdom, and it will be strengthened by prudence.
verses.24:4: Through instruction the storehouses will be filled with all valuable and finest wealth.
verses.24:5: A wise man is strong, and a learned man is sturdy and mighty;
verses.24:6: for war is undertaken with orderly planning, and there will be deliverance where counsels are many.
verses.24:7: Wisdom is too lofty for a fool; at the gate he will not open his mouth.
verses.24:8: He who plans to do evil will be called a fool.
verses.24:9: A fool's planning is sin, and a slanderer is an abomination to people.
verses.24:10: If you despair, weary in the day of distress, your strength will be diminished.
verses.24:11: Rescue those who are being led to death, and do not cease to free those who are being dragged to destruction.
verses.24:12: If you say, "Strength does not suffice," He who is the observer of the heart, He Himself understands; and nothing escapes the keeper of your soul, and He will repay a man according to his works.
verses.24:13: My son, eat honey, for it is good, and the honeycomb, which is sweetest to your throat.
verses.24:14: Such also is the instruction of wisdom for your soul; when you find it, you will have hope in the end, and your hope will not perish.
verses.24:15: Do not lie in wait and seek wickedness in the house of the righteous, nor lay waste his resting place.
verses.24:16: For a righteous man will fall seven times and will rise again, but the wicked will collapse into evil.
verses.24:17: When your enemy falls, do not rejoice, and in his ruin do not let your heart exult,
verses.24:18: or else the Lord may see it, and it may displease Him, and He may take His anger away from him.
verses.24:19: Do not contend with the most evil men, nor envy the wicked;
verses.24:20: for the evil have no hope of things to come, and the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
verses.24:21: Fear the Lord, my son, and the king, and do not mingle with slanderers;
verses.24:22: for their destruction will rise up suddenly, and who knows the ruin of both?
verses.24:23: These things also are for the wise. To favor a person in judgment is not good.
verses.24:24: Peoples will curse those who say to the wicked, "You are righteous," and tribes will detest them.
verses.24:25: Those who rebuke him will be praised, and a blessing will come upon them.
verses.24:26: He who answers with right words will kiss the lips.
verses.24:27: Prepare your work outside, and diligently cultivate your field, so that afterward you may build your house.
verses.24:28: Do not be a witness without cause against your neighbor, nor entice anyone with your lips.
verses.24:29: Do not say, "Just as he did to me, so I will do to him; I will repay each one according to his work."
verses.24:30: I passed through the field of a lazy man, and through the vineyard of a foolish man,
verses.24:31: and look, nettles had completely filled it, and thorns had covered its surface, and the wall of stones had been broken down.
verses.24:32: When I had seen this, I placed it in my heart, and from the example I learned discipline.
verses.24:33: A little, I say, you will sleep, a short while you will slumber; for a tiny moment you will fold your hands so that you may rest,
verses.24:34: and poverty will come to you like a runner, and beggary like an armed man.
verses.25:1: These too are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah, transcribed.
verses.25:2: The glory of God is to conceal a word, and the glory of kings is to investigate a saying.
verses.25:3: Heaven above, and earth below, and the heart of kings is inscrutable.
verses.25:4: Remove the rust from silver, and a completely pure vessel will emerge.
verses.25:5: Remove ungodliness from the face of the king, and his throne will be made firm by righteousness.
verses.25:6: Do not appear boastful before the king, and do not stand in the place of the great.
verses.25:7: For it is better that you be told, "Come up here," than that you be humbled before a prince.
verses.25:8: What your eyes have seen, do not quickly bring out in a dispute, or afterward you may not be able to correct it when you have dishonored your friend.
verses.25:9: Discuss your case with your friend, and do not reveal a secret to an outsider,
verses.25:10: or else he might insult you when he hears it and not stop reproaching you. Favor and friendship deliver; preserve them for yourself, so that you do not become an object of reproach.
verses.25:11: Golden apples on silver beds: such is one who speaks a word in its own time.
verses.25:12: A golden earring and a gleaming pearl: such is one who reproves a wise man and an obedient ear.
verses.25:13: Just as the coldness of snow in the day of harvest, so is a faithful envoy to the one who sent him; he causes his soul to rest.
verses.25:14: Clouds and wind, with rain that does not follow: such is a boastful man who does not fulfill his promises.
verses.25:15: Through patience a prince will be pacified, and a gentle tongue will shatter hardness.
verses.25:16: You have found honey: eat what is enough for you, or else, having had your fill, you might vomit it up.
verses.25:17: Draw back your foot from your neighbor's house, or else someday, having had his fill, he might hate you.
verses.25:18: A javelin, a sword, and a sharp arrow: such is a man who speaks false testimony against his neighbor.
verses.25:19: A rotten tooth and a weary foot: such is one who puts his hope in an unfaithful man in the day of distress,
verses.25:20: and loses his cloak in the day of cold. Vinegar on soda: such is one who sings songs to a wicked heart. Just as a moth does to a garment and a worm to wood, so a man's sorrow harms the heart.
verses.25:21: If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him water to drink;
verses.25:22: for you will gather glowing coals on his head, and the Lord will repay you.
verses.25:23: The north wind dispels rain, and a gloomy face dispels a slandering tongue.
verses.25:24: It is better to sit in a corner of the rooftop than with a contentious woman and in a shared house.
verses.25:25: Cold water to a thirsty soul, and a good report from a distant land.
verses.25:26: A spring muddied by a foot and a polluted wellspring: such is a righteous man falling before an ungodly man.
verses.25:27: Just as it is not good for one who eats much honey, so one who is a scrutinizer of majesty will be crushed by glory.
verses.25:28: Just as a city lying open and without a ring of walls, so is a man who cannot restrain his spirit in speaking.
verses.26:1: Just as snow in summer and rain in harvest, so glory is unfitting for a fool.
verses.26:2: Just as a bird flying away to other places and a sparrow going wherever it wishes, so a curse uttered in vain will come upon someone.
verses.26:3: A whip for a horse, and a halter for a donkey, and a rod on the back of the imprudent.
verses.26:4: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, so that you do not become like him.
verses.26:5: Answer a fool according to his folly, so that he does not seem wise to himself.
verses.26:6: Lame in his feet and drinking iniquity: such is one who sends words through a foolish messenger.
verses.26:7: Just as a lame man has handsome legs in vain, so a proverb is unfitting in the mouth of fools.
verses.26:8: Just as one who throws a stone onto a heap of Mercury, so is one who grants honor to an unwise man.
verses.26:9: Just as if a thorn should sprout in the hand of a drunkard, so is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
verses.26:10: Judgment settles cases, and one who imposes silence on a fool calms anger.
verses.26:11: Just as a dog that returns to its vomit, so is an imprudent man who repeats his folly.
verses.26:12: Have you seen a man who seems wise to himself? An unwise man will have more hope than he.
verses.26:13: The lazy man says, "There is a lion on the road, and a lioness on the paths."
verses.26:14: Just as a door turns on its hinge, so does the lazy man on his bed.
verses.26:15: The lazy man hides his hand under his armpit, and he labors if he turns it to his mouth.
verses.26:16: The lazy man seems wiser to himself than seven men speaking maxims.
verses.26:17: Just as one who seizes a dog by the ears, so is one who passes by impatiently and gets mixed up in another's quarrel.
verses.26:18: Just as one who launches arrows and spears to bring death is harmful,
verses.26:19: so a man deceitfully harms his friend, and when he has been caught, he says, "I did it in play."
verses.26:20: When the wood runs out, the fire will be extinguished, and with the whisperer removed, disputes will quiet down.
verses.26:21: Just as charcoal is to glowing coals and wood to fire, so a hot-tempered man stirs up quarrels.
verses.26:22: The words of a whisperer are seemingly simple, and they penetrate to the depths of the belly.
verses.26:23: Just as if you wanted to adorn a clay vessel with impure silver, so are swelling lips allied with a wicked heart.
verses.26:24: By his lips an enemy is recognized, when he has plotted deceits in his heart.
verses.26:25: When he lowers his voice, do not trust him, because seven evils are in his heart.
verses.26:26: One who covers hatred deceitfully will have his malice revealed in the council.
verses.26:27: One who digs a pit will fall into it, and for one who rolls a stone, it will return to him.
verses.26:28: A deceitful tongue does not love truth, and a slippery mouth produces ruin.
verses.27:1: Do not boast about tomorrow, not knowing what the coming day may produce.
verses.27:2: Let another person praise you, and not your mouth; a stranger, and not your lips.
verses.27:3: A rock is heavy and sand is burdensome, but a fool's anger is heavier than both.
verses.27:4: Anger has no mercy, nor does bursting fury; and who will be able to endure the onslaught of one who is stirred up?
verses.27:5: An open rebuke is better than concealed love.
verses.27:6: Better are the wounds of one who loves than the deceitful kisses of one who hates.
verses.27:7: A sated soul will trample a honeycomb, and a hungry soul will take even what is bitter as sweet.
verses.27:8: Just as a bird migrating from its nest, so is a man who abandons his place.
verses.27:9: The heart is delighted by ointment and various fragrances, and the soul is sweetened by a friend's good counsels.
verses.27:10: Do not abandon your friend and your father's friend, and do not enter your brother's house on the day of your affliction. Better is a neighbor close by than a brother far away.
verses.27:11: Devote yourself to wisdom, my son, and gladden my heart, so that you may be able to answer a word to one who reproaches.
verses.27:12: A shrewd man, seeing evil, has hidden himself; little ones, passing on, have suffered losses.
verses.27:13: Take the garment of the one who has become guarantor for a stranger, and for outsiders take a pledge from him.
verses.27:14: Whoever blesses his neighbor with a loud voice, rising during the night, will be like one who curses.
verses.27:15: Dripping roofs on a day of cold and a quarrelsome woman are comparable.
verses.27:16: The one who restrains her is like someone who would hold the wind, and he will summon the oil of his right hand.
verses.27:17: Iron is sharpened by iron, and a man sharpens the face of his friend.
verses.27:18: Whoever watches over a fig tree will eat its fruits, and the one who is the keeper of his master will be honored.
verses.27:19: Just as in waters the faces of those looking in shine back, so the hearts of people are evident to the prudent.
verses.27:20: Hell and destruction are never filled; likewise, the eyes of people are also insatiable.
